experiment.name: early_power_reveal
experiment.change: Explicitly state the hero's core power or identity within the first three shots immediately following the hook.
experiment.rationale: Establishing the protagonist's specific stakes and abilities early will ground viewer context before the main conflict escalates.

experiment.name: sensory_onomatopoeia_emphasis
experiment.change: Incorporate at least one onomatopoeia sound effect from the comic panel directly into the narration text of that shot.
experiment.rationale: Adding sensory sound words to the narration increases engagement by mimicking the comic book reading experience.

experiment.name: ultra_short_middle_shot
experiment.change: Include exactly one 2-word shot in the middle of the video to create a sharp pacing drop.
experiment.rationale: Sudden rhythm shifts keep viewer retention high on YouTube Shorts by disrupting predictability.

experiment.name: dialogue_hook
experiment.change: Start the hook with a direct quote from a speech balloon in the first panel.
experiment.rationale: Using an in-world quote immediately immerses the viewer into the action faster than third-person exposition.

experiment.name: color_coded_keywords
experiment.change: Highlight key nouns in yellow to draw visual focus to plot-critical objects in the captions.
experiment.rationale: Color-coding key nouns helps viewers quickly grasp the central conflict and objects of interest in fast-paced Shorts.

experiment.name: tighter_duration_target
experiment.change: Cap total video duration under 45 seconds by keeping narration strictly between 80 and 110 words total.
experiment.rationale: Shorter Golden Age recaps prevent mid-video drop-off and boost completion rate on YouTube Shorts.

experiment.name: action_verb_titles
experiment.change: Use an imperative action verb at the start of the title to heighten immediate curiosity.
experiment.rationale: Starting titles with high-energy action verbs can boost initial click-through rates on short-form feeds.

experiment.name: question_hook
experiment.change: Start the hook with a direct question addressing the viewer to boost initial engagement.
experiment.rationale: Direct questions create a cognitive open loop that forces viewers to watch further to find the answer.

experiment.name: color_coded_captions
experiment.change: Use blue text for hero dialogue and white text for narrator narration.
experiment.rationale: Differentiating speaker types visually helps viewers follow the narrative flow faster.

experiment.name: cliffhanger_transitions
experiment.change: End the penultimate shot with a question that is answered by the final image.
experiment.rationale: Cliffhangers encourage viewers to watch the final frame, increasing retention.

experiment.name: strict_emphasis_ratio
experiment.change: Limit visual emphasis (red, green, cyan) to exactly one in every four shots.
experiment.rationale: Standardizing visual cues prevents viewer fatigue and ensures high-impact moments remain distinct.

experiment.name: ultra_short_beats
experiment.change: Cap every single shot's narration at a maximum of 4 words to maximize hyper-fast YouTube Shorts pacing.
experiment.rationale: Shorter beats increase retention and align better with rapid-fire word-by-word caption styles.

experiment.name: concise_hook
experiment.change: Limit the hook question to a maximum of 6 words.
experiment.rationale: Shorter, punchier hook questions capture viewer attention faster in the first 2 seconds.

experiment.name: cliffhanger_penultimate_shot
experiment.change: The second-to-last shot must be a narrator question in white text, followed by a silent 2-second final panel showing the visual answer.
experiment.rationale: Creating a brief moment of silence for the visual payoff can increase the impact of the consequence and improve loop-back retention.

experiment.name: hero_first_word_hook
experiment.change: Start the hook question with the superhero's full name as the first two words.
experiment.rationale: Leading immediately with a recognizable hero name increases instant viewer familiarity and retention.

experiment.name: two_character_dialogue_shots
experiment.change: Include at least two shots containing hero dialogue transcribed verbatim from speech balloons and rendered with blue captions.
experiment.rationale: Direct character speech breaks up third-person narration and leverages the highest-performing video's color-coded caption mechanic to boost retention.

experiment.name: midpoint_twist_reveal_beat
experiment.change: Place a single green-emphasized plot reveal shot exactly at the midpoint (shots 14-16) of the narration arc.
experiment.rationale: Anchoring a major narrative turning point at the exact midpoint prevents mid-video retention drop-offs in 120-second formats.

experiment.name: red_danger_hook_emphasis
experiment.change: Ensure the first shot (hook) always uses red danger emphasis on the primary threat words.
experiment.rationale: High-performing videos leverage early danger signals to immediately draw viewers in during the first 2 seconds.
